The Real, with its uproarious richness, is a casualty of those fixated so doggedly on goodness; innocence and naivety hold the dripping sword. The Real remains ever whole and spritely; though in the hearts of the innocent, it is severed, to a point - less so, I admit, than in the truly heartless. Perhaps it is my own naivety which slackens my hope in view of such puerile comportment; I cannot fathom the sundering of a soul from the dark truths of Kali Yuga, and Kali's black light shines so brightly for me that I may be blinded to the truth that it is too her caprice that shades and protects so many pure hearted ones. Though whether this mock-safety is truly a protection is the worry that riles me, and rules over the discontent I feel in even the most joyous and benevolent of atmospheres. For I know that Kali will and must have her day, and the sooner you let her dawn upon you, the lesser the suffering that the false sun of our lulling summer night will cultivate in statu nascendi, quakingly awaiting with eyes averted her invigorating rays which are the birthing of destruction, inner and outer. That her destruction is a blessing remains the hardest and most forlorn communique left subjugated within my locked, wavering lips, but I can only give her my faith that she, as consort of the most high intelligence and artistry, will bring peace to all, or rather, bring all to Peace, with deft, ravening aplomb, dancing life, with the Dionyasian reverie of the dervish, to death and beyond, in life and in the next. The part I may play must land in my lap, and it is my karma to shoulder the wait; these sub realities born of paucity of perception and conception are to be, it seems, my perplexing penance, duly held I might add. The poet that is bard to the universe most surely knows, with archetypal exactitude, the minutiae of meanings that spell out Time's living out and living through death.
